items.prompt: Put the incident response steps in order.
items.explanation: Contain first so the damage stops, then clean up and recover. The report at the end stops the same incident from happening again.

items.prompt: Yudi's account was broken into and used to send malware to every employee. The right containment step is…
choices: Reset Yudi's password and pull back the email with the attachment
items.explanation: Containing means cutting off the attacker's access and stopping the spread, without breaking anything else.

choices: Only when you're 100% sure it's an attack
When the incident affects many people, or you're unsure
Never, analysts must solve it on their own
items.explanation: Escalating quickly lets the right team take action. Being unsure is a valid reason to escalate.

items.prompt: Why is the "report & learn" step still important after the system has recovered?
choices: So the same incident doesn't happen again
So there is someone to blame
It's not important once the system has recovered
items.explanation: Lessons from an incident are used to improve rules and training. The goal is to prevent, not to blame.
